$comment: Every environment variable and secret the gamedev-app service is given, declared once.
Two supported deploy paths thread this map independently: .github/workflows/deploy.yml
and infra/deploy-api.sh. gcloud's --set-env-vars replaces the WHOLE map, so a variable
present in one path and absent from the other is not a partial config — it is silently
deleted the next time the other path runs. That is not hypothetical: on 2026-08-04 a
hand-set TRANSLATE_BUILD_LOG=false stopped a Vertex spend leak, then vanished under an
unrelated deploy ten minutes later and the leak resumed unnoticed (infra/deploy-api.sh).
infra/check-env-manifest.mjs asserts both paths thread exactly the names below, and runs
as part of `npm run lint`. Adding a variable to one path alone now fails CI instead of
reverting itself in production months later.
Adding a variable: add it here AND to both deploy paths in the same change.
Removing one: delete it from all three, and check nothing in apps/api still reads it.
Names that look like service variables in one of the deploy files but are not, so
the checker must not demand them from the other path. Each needs a reason: this is
the escape hatch, and an unexplained entry here is how a real divergence hides.
INVITE_URL earned its place by being threaded to Cloud Run for months while only
the beta:invite / beta:welcome CLIs ever read it.
notServiceVars.CANDIDATE_URL: step-local: the untrafficked revision URL the smoke tests curl
notServiceVars.E2E_CHROMIUM_PATH: step-local: where the browser gate finds Chromium on the runner
notServiceVars.MP_RELAY_URL_VAL: step-local: shell variable behind MP_RELAY_URL, not its own var
notServiceVars.FLAG_VAL: step-local: loop scratch variable in infra/deploy-api.sh
notServiceVars.INVITE_URL: read only by the beta:invite and beta:welcome CLIs on the operator's machine, never by the service
